Award types: what is actually in the data

Source: vignettes/award-types.Rmd
award-types.Rmd
library(usaspend)

Every transaction carries an award type code, and the code determines whether its dollars are revenue, capacity, or someone else’s money. The package’s taxonomy:

us_award_type_codes()
#>  [1] "A"       "B"       "C"       "D"       "IDV_A"   "IDV_B"   "IDV_B_A" "IDV_B_B"
#>  [9] "IDV_B_C" "IDV_C"   "IDV_D"   "IDV_E"   "02"      "03"      "04"      "05"     
#> [17] "06"      "10"      "07"      "08"      "09"      "11"

Each code maps to an award_family (grant, contract, idv, direct_payment, loan, other) and an award_group (assistance vs contract — which of USAspending’s two file layouts it arrives in).

What a real portfolio looks like

The 50-nonprofit pilot (302,025 transactions, FY2008–FY2025), by type:

type rows dollars what it actually is revenue?
Project grants (04) + coop agreements (05) 212k $62.8bn the core yes
Contracts (A–D) 56.6k $76.4bn delivery orders, definitive contracts, POs, BPA calls yes
Direct payments (06, 10) 19.3k $3.0bn almost entirely Pell, work-study, SEOG — student aid moving through the institution separable; usually exclude
Direct loans (07) 6.5k $0 obligated, $626bn face value Federal Direct Student Loans; the university is a conduit face value never
Formula/block grants (03, 02) 2.1k $1.6bn mostly government-affiliated orgs yes
Other/reimbursable (11) 1.2k $0.3bn DOE/DOD/USDA cooperative R&D revenue-like
IDVs 4.3k ~$0.8bn obligated vs $115bn ceiling contract vehicles obligations only

Two numbers carry the whole argument: $626bn of loan face value and $115bn of IDV ceiling, against $118.5bn of actual net obligations. Summing the wrong dollar column overstates this portfolio roughly sixfold.

Loans: the data gets it right, keep it that way

Every type-07 row in the pilot is a Federal Direct Student Loan. The loans are to students; the institution originates them. USAspending already encodes this correctly — federal_action_obligation is $0 on every one, and the face value travels in its own column (loan_face_value in the panel). The rule is simply to never let face value or subsidy cost reach a revenue total. Direct payments (06, 10) are the same story one step removed — student aid booked to the school but economically the students’ — so they stay in the ledger with award_family = "direct_payment", and a nonprofit-revenue analysis usually filters them out explicitly.

IDVs: vehicles, not money

An indefinite-delivery vehicle (GWAC, IDC, BPA, BOA, FSS) is a contract container. Its ceiling is capacity; the money is obligated on the delivery orders placed under it — which are separate awards with their own keys. The sample shows the pair:

tx <- us_sample_extract()$transactions
tx[grepl("HHSD200200720032I", award_key),
   .(rows = .N, obligated = sum(federal_action_obligation)),
   by = .(award_key, award_type_label)]
#>                                                    award_key award_type_label  rows
#>                                                       <char>           <char> <int>
#> 1:                           CONT_IDV_HHSD200200720032I_7523              IDC     7
#> 2: CONT_AWD_HHSD2002007200320001_7523_HHSD200200720032I_7523   Delivery Order     6
#> 3: CONT_AWD_HHSD2002007200320002_7523_HHSD200200720032I_7523   Delivery Order     7
#> 4: CONT_AWD_HHSD2002007200320003_7523_HHSD200200720032I_7523   Delivery Order     8
#> 5: CONT_AWD_HHSD2002007200320004_7523_HHSD200200720032I_7523   Delivery Order     5
#>    obligated
#>        <num>
#> 1:       0.0
#> 2:  281586.3
#> 3:  390297.9
#> 4: 1818651.0
#> 5:  458210.1

The vehicle: $0 across its own modifications, against a $40M potential value. The delivery orders under it: the actual obligations. Whether to roll delivery orders up into their parent vehicle is a modelling choice — it changes award counts and agency attribution, not dollar totals — and the package defaults to not rolling up.

Two traps the package absorbs so you don’t hit them

Codes collide across families. B is Continuation for assistance and Supplemental Agreement for contracts; C is Revision vs Funding Only Action; D is Adjustment to Completed Award vs Change Order. Any classification that ignores award_group is wrong, which is why us_classify_action() requires it:

us_classify_action(c("B", "C"), award_group = "assistance")[, -1]
#>    action_type_code action_type_label action_class
#>              <char>            <char>       <char>
#> 1:                B      Continuation continuation
#> 2:                C          Revision     revision
us_classify_action(c("B", "C"), award_group = "contract")[, -1]
#>    action_type_code                   action_type_label action_class
#>              <char>                              <char>       <char>
#> 1:                B Supplemental Agreement Within Scope     revision
#> 2:                C                 Funding Only Action funding_only

Description strings are not stable — group on codes, never labels. The same pull can carry "DELIVERY ORDER" and "DO" for one code, and archive files carry different strings again (vignette("acquisition")). Package labels are always derived from the code via us_classify_award_type(), so they are stable no matter what the source file said. Contract IDV rows add one more wrinkle: their award_type_code is blank and the type lives in idv_type_code as a bare letter, which the classifier prefixes ("B" → "IDV_B") because bare "B" would read as Purchase Order.
